dedupe_keys.name: bgs mineral planning permissions and historic mhlg permission maps england

description: These two BGS datasets map the extent of planning permissions for mineral extraction. Mineral Planning Permissions shows all known extant and non-extant permissions, whatever their current status, including active, inactive and restored workings and permitted but unworked deposits; it was compiled mainly from data supplied by Mineral Planning Authorities, and although the entry title says England 1997 to 2007, the text describes coverage of Great Britain. The historic land use dataset digitises about 1,400 paper maps at 1:25 000 and a card index received from the government between 2001 and 2003, compiled by the Minerals Division of the Ministry of Housing and Local Government, with hand-drawn boundaries of permitted, withdrawn and refused permissions, worked ground and land use from the 1940s (back to 1930) to the mid 1980s, for England only. Access: data.gov.uk lists copyright as vested in NERC with reuse needing BGS permission; format and price are not stated on the pages read. Caveats: permitted reserves may be depleted to any degree, and the historic maps were hand drawn. For simulation it shows where extraction is permitted now and in the past, useful for aggregate supply planning and for finding old workings under present infrastructure. Related catalogue records include BGS BritPits and BGS Mining Hazard (not including coal).
